title: Regional fallback matrix and exception flows
content:
Purpose:
This doc defines a compact, operator-friendly fallback matrix and exception flows for Private deployments when region-pin requirements interact with capacity constraints, outages, or cross-border regulatory exceptions. Goal: give SREs and deployment engineers a decision checklist, exact fallback rules, and sample commands to apply safe temporary workarounds while preserving auditability and compliance signals.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to: Redwood Private (VPC + on-prem) and Dedicated routing that supports region pinning and model variants.
- Not covered: hosted multi-tenant endpoints (handled by hosted-api runbooks).
- Assumes customer has declared one of: strict-sovereign (no egress), soft-sovereign (data may egress under encryption + consent), or opt-in-fallback (customer allows fallback by SLA).

Summary of the matrix (operator quick view):

1) Strict-sovereign (legal block on egress):
   - Normal: Enforce hard pin to region. Reject requests if local capacity exhausted.
   - Fallback: NO automatic fallback. Manual exception only via legal-approved ticket.
   - Audit: Generate incident with tag residency:strict and record decision reason.

2) Soft-sovereign (allowed egress with safeguards):
   - Normal: Prefer local region; if capacity breached, route to remote region with encryption-in-flight + split-logging.
   - Fallback: Route to pre-approved region variant (same legal jurisdiction if available), else to 'bordered' region with additional masking.
   - Audit: Log egress event with customer consent id and redaction hash.

3) Opt-in-fallback (customer enabled emergency fallback):
   - Normal: Local first, then fallback automatically to next-region candidate when latency SLA violated or capacity exhausted.
   - Fallback: Use cached/KV-only responses when possible; otherwise route to fallback region.
   - Audit: Note SLA-breach-driven fallback and fallback-region id.

Decision flow (high-level):
- Step 0: Incoming request carries header X-REDWOOD-RESIDENCY: strict|soft|opt-in and pin_region tag.
- Step 1: Check local pool capacity and model-compatibility.
- Step 2: If local capacity OK -> serve locally.
- Step 3: If not OK -> consult residency policy for customer.
   - strict -> return 451 (Region-Lock) + remediation link.
   - soft -> check allowed-fallback-list -> route if allowed.
   - opt-in -> consult failover chain (ordered list) and route to highest-priority candidate that meets model/latency constraints.
- Step 4: Emit residency event to AuditLog service and attach fallback rationale tag.

Operational knobs and required telemetry:
- Per-customer policy: allowed_fallback_regions (ordered list), fallback_mode (cache-only | full), consent_id (if required), legal_exception_ticket (nullable).
- Metrics to emit: residency_fallback_count, residency_block_count, residency_latency_trigger_count, fallback_region_histogram.
- Tracing spans: mark span attribute residency.policy_applied and residency.fallback_reason.

Fallback candidate selection heuristic (short):
- Must match model variant (quantization/precision) OR have compatible runtime shim.
- Prefer same legal jurisdiction by country code.
- Lowest estimated added latency (based on edge-tracer + last-24h p95).
- If two candidates tie, prefer region with available KV-cache footprint for the customer.

Emergency operator actions (cheat-sheet):
1) Immediate capacity failure in strict-sovereign region (customer allowed NO egress):
   - Command: open ticket to security & legal (use template) -> CONSUMER-TICKET-RESIDENCY.
   - If customer agrees to temporary soft fallback, capture consent_id and set policy: allowed_fallback_regions=[eu-west-1], fallback_mode=full via admin console.
   - Rollback: revert allowed_fallback_regions and record reason.

2) Soft-sovereign region overloaded, need temporary relief:
   - Step A: Attempt transparent cache-serve: --enable-prefix-cache for customer's model-set (CLI snippet below).
   - CLI snippet: redwoodctl cache enable --customer-id c123 --model family/x    
   - If cache insufficient, apply routing override (10 min window):
     - UI: Deployment -> Customer -> Routing Overrides -> Add fallback eu-west-1 priority 10 window 600s
     - Or CLI: redwoodctl routing override --customer c123 --target-region eu-west-1 --ttl 600 --reason "soft-fallback-10min"

3) Automated opt-in fallback triggered repeatedly (rate > threshold):
   - Create paging event for infra capacity team.
   - Add a canary weight reduction on heavy routes: rollout: canary 20% -> shift 5% every 10m.

Audit log and evidence capture (must-haves):
- For any non-local serve, persist: customer_id, policy_type, fallback_region, consent_id (if present), operator_id (if manual change), ticket_id, previous_policy_snapshot (JSON blob id).
- Export periodic CSV for compliance reviewers with residency decisions for last 30 days.

Example decision matrix text table (for quick copy-paste):

| Policy | Auto-fallback allowed? | Preferred candidate | Temp operator action | Audit tag |
| strict | NO | n/a | open legal ticket | residency:strict |
| soft | YES | same-jurisdiction -> bordered-region -> cache-only | routing override / enable-cache | residency:soft |
| opt-in | YES | ordered failover chain from customer's policy | automatic + oncall alert | residency:optin |

Unresolved questions / TODOs (needs follow-up):
- Q1: How to represent consent_id lifecycle so it is cryptographically tamper-evident and queryable by auditors? (idea: sign consent blob and store hash in AuditLog).
- Q2: Should we expose an opt-in 'latency budget' field that customers can configure (e.g., allow fallback if estimated p95 added latency < X ms)?
- Q3: SLA billing implications when fallback crosses into a paid cross-region egress — clear billing flags need to be added to customer invoices.
- Q4: Backfill strategy for cached responses when routing to remote region to avoid cold-start quality regressions.

Runbook snippets (operator copy-and-paste):
- Mark incident and tag: /inc create "residency-fallback-{customer}" --tag residency --priority p2
- Route override via CLI: redwoodctl routing override --customer c123 --source-region ap-southeast-1 --target-region ap-southeast-2 --ttl 900 --reason "auto-fallback-pressing-queue"
- Revoke override: redwoodctl routing override revoke --id <override-id>
- Snapshot current policy: redwoodctl residency snapshot --customer c123 > /var/tmp/c123-policy-$(date +%F).json

Audit and compliance checklist for reviewers:
- Verify every fallback has an associated audit record within 5 minutes.
- Validate consent_id presence for soft-fallback rows.
- Confirm manual overrides have operator and ticket references.

Communication templates (for CS/Legal to use when asking customers):
- Short consent request: "We are experiencing regional capacity constraints in <region>. To avoid request failures, may we temporarily route your traffic to <candidate-region> under encrypted transport for up to <ttl> minutes? Reply YES to confirm. Consent-id will be recorded for audit"
- Emergency rollback notice: "We reverted a temporary routing override for your deployment in <region> at <timestamp>. If you experience issues, please contact support@redwood.ai with ticket <ticket-id>."

Appendix A: sample audit event (human readable form)
- event_id: ev-20260110-0001
- customer: c123
- policy: soft
- action: routed -> eu-west-1
- reason: local-pool-exhausted
- operator: lina.sre
- ticket: ENG-OPS-1427
- consent_id: consent-20260110-87ab

Notes and provenance:
- Based on weekly residency synthesis with product & legal (notes in linked confluence page), feedback from solutions-eng pilots (Sep-Oct 2025), and infra capacity reports (Q4 2025).
- This doc is intentionally operational and concise — long-form policy lives in Confluence (see linked_artifacts).

Next steps (owners):
- [Priya] Draft consent_id signing proposal (due 2026-02-07).
- [Rakesh] Wire metric residency_fallback_count into observability dashboard (due 2026-01-25).
- [Sofia] Add billing flag on fallback events to invoices repo (PR by 2026-02-14).

If you are oncall and unsure: ping @liam.oconnor on Slack or escalate through the normal SRE rotation.
